# 03-review-binding-redirects: Review Framework assembly binding redirects

Review and document the binding redirects associated with the three Framework projects before any are removed during TFM migration. The assessment flags 61 binding issues, including mandatory redirect coverage and version conflicts; record the purpose and disposition of redirects that affect package/runtime behavior, and distinguish redirects that can be dropped with the Framework runtime from configuration needed during the staged conversion.

**Done when**: Redirects and their identified conflicts have a documented disposition before cleanup; no redirect is removed without review; and the project/configuration owners for unresolved runtime concerns are identified.

## Research Findings
- Inspected the three SDK-style `net48` project files and their adjacent `app.config` files. The two desktop projects have `UseWPF` and `UseWindowsForms`; only `StockAnalyzerApp` is an executable. `StockAnalyzerLib/app.config` and `StockAnalyzerSettings/app.config` do not become runtime config files for the host executable; `StockAnalyzerApp/app.config` is the app's configuration source. No config was edited in this review task.
- Redirect inventory: `StockAnalyzer/app.config` (library config) has 10 redirects; `StockAnalyzerApp/app.config` (app config) has 14; `StockAnalyzerSettings/app.config` has none. All three configs declare `.NETFramework,Version=v4.8` startup metadata.
- `StockAnalyzerLib.csproj` and `StockAnalyzerSettings.csproj` both set `AutoGenerateBindingRedirects=false`. Assessment identifies one mandatory `Binding.0001` issue for Settings (disabled auto-generation with no manual redirects), `Binding.0002` partial redirects and `Binding.0008` insufficient Unsafe coverage for Lib. The app config has manual redirects; assessment reports 10 `Binding.0006` MSB3836 conflicts and 11 downgrade/version mismatch warnings, plus missing redirect coverage for package/runtime references.
- The app retains ClickOnce-related properties (`PublishUrl`, `GenerateManifests`, and manifest configuration) and application/user settings. Do not remove or rewrite the full `app.config` merely because .NET 10 does not use .NET Framework Fusion redirects: preserve application settings/service-model sections, and separately validate publishing/runtime configuration during the app migration.
- `StockAnalyzerSettings` uses generated `Properties.Settings` values, and the app uses its own generated settings. The library also consumes Settings defaults. Any move/consolidation of settings sections during migration must preserve existing user/application settings behavior; this review does not relocate those sections.

## Redirect Inventory and Disposition
### `StockAnalyzer/app.config` (10; library project config, not host executable config)
- `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe`: `0.0.0.0-6.0.0.0` → `6.0.0.0`. Incorrect/insufficient: the referenced package requires assembly `6.0.3.0`; assessment Binding.0008 is mandatory and Binding.0007 flags downgrade. Do not carry into net10 as a Fusion redirect; verify actual resolved package assets when migrating Lib.
- `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions`: `0.0.0.0-4.2.4.0` → `4.2.4.0`; `System.Buffers`: `0.0.0.0-4.0.5.0` → `4.0.5.0`; `System.Memory`: `0.0.0.0-4.0.5.0` → `4.0.5.0`. These target older assembly versions than current package assets (4.6.3 / 4.6.1); assessment flags downgrades/missing coverage. Do not copy as-is to net10; runtime package resolution must be validated after retarget.
- `System.Text.Encodings.Web`, `System.Text.Json`, `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces`, `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`, `Microsoft.Bcl.TimeProvider`: each redirects `0.0.0.0-10.0.0.2` → `10.0.0.2`, while package metadata is 10.0.2. Stale Framework-era redirects; no Fusion redirect is needed for net10, but package alignment/runtime smoke validation remains necessary.

### `StockAnalyzerApp/app.config` (14; application config)
- `Newtonsoft.Json`: `0.0.0.0-13.0.0.0` → `13.0.0.0`; app package is 13.0.4, producing Binding.0006 conflict and Binding.0007 mismatch. Keep app settings/config sections; discard only the obsolete Fusion redirect on net10 after package runtime validation.
- `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe`: `0.0.0.0-6.0.3.0` → `6.0.3.0`; app package is 6.1.2 and Lib's package is 6.1.2. Assessment reports MSB3836 conflict and version mismatch. Do not preserve stale redirect in the net10 host; validate resolved package assets.
- `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions`: `0.0.0.0-4.2.4.0` → `4.2.4.0`; `System.Buffers`: `0.0.0.0-4.0.5.0` → `4.0.5.0`; `System.Memory`: `0.0.0.0-4.0.5.0` → `4.0.5.0`; `System.Numerics.Vectors`: `0.0.0.0-4.1.6.0` → `4.1.6.0`. Target old assembly versions versus packages 4.6.3 / 4.6.1; Binding.0006/0007 mismatches are not to be resolved by keeping stale net48 redirects.
- `System.Text.Encodings.Web`, `System.Text.Json`, `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces`, `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource`, `System.IO.Pipelines`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`, `Microsoft.Bcl.TimeProvider`: redirects target 10.0.0.2 while packages are 10.0.2, resulting in MSB3836 conflicts or downgrade reports. Do not migrate these redirects into net10 runtime configuration; preserve non-Fusion app configuration and test package loading.
- `Telerik.Licensing.Runtime`: `0.0.0.0-1.6.31.0` → `1.6.31.0`, but the old hinted DLL was absent and SDK conversion restored the checked-in Telerik 2026 licensing DLL version 1.6.40.0. Assessment flags mismatch. Do not leave this stale redirect in net10; ensure Telerik licensing/control assemblies are all resolved to the checked-in 2026 distribution in the app migration.

### `StockAnalyzerSettings/app.config` (0 redirects)
- No assembly redirects to remove. Preserve its user/application-settings sections and reassess how generated settings are loaded by the net10 host; the `.NETFramework` startup declaration is obsolete after retargeting.

## Task Disposition
- This task is documentation-only: all identified redirects are Framework Fusion policy and are candidates for removal when their owning config is migrated to net10, but actual removal is deferred until tasks 04–06 so application settings, service configuration, Telerik resolution, and package behavior can be handled together.
- Do not remove whole config files or setting sections wholesale. In particular, preserve `StockAnalyzerApp/app.config` user settings and empty WCF `<system.serviceModel>` client/bindings sections until service usage is verified. Review generated .NET 10 runtime config and ClickOnce behavior during the app migration.
- Task 04 owns Settings config migration; task 05 owns the library redirect/reference audit; task 06 owns the application redirect cleanup and settings/publishing validation. `UltimateChartistSync` is unrelated and remains untouched.
